sanskrit: śaṃ no devī pṛśniparṇy aśaṃ nirṛtaye karat | ugrā hi kaṇvajambhanī tāṃ tvāhārṣaṃ sahasvatīm ||
english: Auspicious to us be the goddess Pṛśniparṇī; let her bring ill-fortune to Nirṛti. For she is fierce, the devourer of kaṇva-demons — her, the powerful one, I have fetched for you.

sanskrit: sadānvāghnī prathamā pṛśniparṇy ajāyata | tayā kaṇvasyāhaṃ śiraś chinadmi śakuner iva ||
english: Pṛśniparṇī was born first as one who ever pursues and strikes down. With her I sever the head of kaṇva as one severs the head of a bird.

sanskrit: ūrjabhṛtaṃ prāṇabhṛtaṃ prajānām uta tarpaṇīm | sarvās tāḥ pṛśniparṇī- -itaḥ kaṇvā mā nīnaśat ||
english: She who bears vigor, who bears life-breath, and who is the refresher of living beings — may Pṛśniparṇī drive all those kaṇvas to destruction away from here.

sanskrit: samākṛtyainā nir aja tīkṣṇaśṛṅga iva ṛṣabhaḥ | arāyaṃ kaṇvaṃ pāpmānaṃ pṛśniparṇi sahasvati ||
english: Rounding them up, drive them out as a sharp-horned bull drives out its herd — the greedy kaṇva, the sinful one, O mighty Pṛśniparṇī.

sanskrit: tvam ugre pṛśniparṇy agnir iva pradahann ihi kaṇvā jīvitayopanīḥ | girim enā ā veśaya tamāṃsi yatra gacchāṃs tat pāpīr api pādaya ||
english: You, fierce Pṛśniparṇī, come burning like fire; the kaṇvas have been brought near to the end of life. Drive them into the mountain, into the darkness whither they depart — cast those evil ones down there.

sanskrit: arāyam asṛkpāvānaṃ yaś ca sphātiṃ jihīrṣati | garbhādaṃ kaṇvaṃ nāśaya pṛśniparṇi sahasvati ||
english: The greedy blood-drinker, and the one who desires to steal away prosperity, and the womb-devouring kaṇva — destroy them, O mighty Pṛśniparṇī.

sanskrit: yā no gā yā no gṛhān yā na sphātim upāharān | tā ugre pṛśniparṇi tvaṃ kaṇvā mā nīnaśa itaḥ ||
english: Those kaṇvas who carry off our cattle, who carry off our homes, who carry off our prosperity — those, O fierce Pṛśniparṇī, drive to destruction away from here.

sanskrit: yasminn āśīḥ pratihita idaṃ tac chalyo veṇur veṣṭanaṃ tejanaṃ ca | sūnur janitrīṃ janayehi śṛṇvann ayaṃ ta ātmeta it prahitaḥ ||
english: That in which a spell is implanted — here is that śalya (splinter/shaft), the reed, the wrapping, and the point. As a son hears and comes to his mother, so hear: this is your very self — be thus dislodged.

sanskrit: asthi bhittvā yadi majjñaḥ papātha yadi vāsi rataḥ puruṣantikāme | urvīṃ gavyūtim abhy ehy arvāṅ paścā raśmīn udyataḥ sūryasya ||
english: If, having split the bone, you have fallen into the marrow, or if you are lodged in one who is dear to a woman — come back across the broad cow-pasture ground, following in the track of the rays of the risen sun.

sanskrit: mātariśvā pavamānas tvāyan sūrya ābhrājan tanvā dṛśe kaḥ | asno gandhāt puvasaḥ pra cyavasva vi mucyasva yonyā yā te atra ||
english: Mātariśvan, the purifying wind, blowing along you; the sun shining brightly so the body may be seen — from the smell of blood, from the festering, dislodge yourself; free yourself from the wound that is there in you.

sanskrit: pra cyavasvāto abhy ehy arvāṅ arthāṃs te vidma bahudhā bahir ye | imāḥ svasāro ayam it pitā ta iyaṃ te mātemam ehi bandhum ||
english: Dislodge yourself from there, come back this way; we know your many purposes, those that are outside. These are your sisters, this indeed is your father, this is your mother — come here to this kinsman.

sanskrit: amitrair astā yadi vāsi mitrair devair vā devi prahitāvasṛṣṭā- -āviddhā śṛṅgaṃ puruṣe jahātha | bāṇaḥ śṛṅgaṃ śikharaḥ saṃ satām itaḥ ||
english: Whether you were shot by enemies or by friends, or sent forth and released by gods or by a goddess — having pierced and left the horn in the man, O arrow, let the horn and point be conjoined and depart from here.

sanskrit: śikhāsu sakto yadi vāsy agre yadi vāsi saktaḥ puruṣasya māṃse | dadhṛṅ na pāśām̐ apavṛjya muktvā- -akṣiśalyaḥ kṛṇutām āyanāya ||
english: If you are lodged among the tips, or lodged at the front, or lodged in the flesh of a man — like one who looses a noose and sets free the fetter, let the splinter from the eye make its way for departure.

sanskrit: hastād dhastaṃ sam ayo bhriyamāṇo bahiṣ ṭvā paśyān vīrudhāṃ balena | adbhiḥ praṇiktaḥ śayāsā abhyaktaḥ kośe jāmīnāṃ nihito ahiṃsaḥ ||
english: Carried from hand to hand, the metal may see you out by the power of healing plants; cleansed with waters, anointed as one lying down, placed harmless in the sheath of the kinswomen.

sanskrit: ṣaṣṭirātre ṣaṣṭikasya śalyasya paridhiṣ kṛtaḥ | itas tam adya te vayam āsthānāc cyāvayāmasi ||
english: For the sixty-fold śalya an enclosure of sixty nights has been made. Today we dislodge it from its station away from here for you.

sanskrit: saṃ majjā majjñā bhavatu sam u te paruṣā paruḥ | saṃ te rāṣṭrasya visrastaṃ saṃ snāva sam u parva te ||
english: Let marrow be joined with marrow; let joint be united with joint for you. Let that which has been scattered of your bodily frame come together; let sinew and let joint be joined for you.

sanskrit: majjā majjñā saṃ dhīyatām asthnāsthy api rohatu | snāva te saṃ dadhmaḥ snāvnā carmaṇā carma rohatu ||
english: Let marrow be laid together with marrow; let bone grow upon bone. We bind your sinew together with sinew; let skin grow upon skin.

sanskrit: loma lomnā saṃ dhīyatāṃ tvacā saṃ kalpayāt tvacam | asṛk te asnā rohatu māṃsaṃ māṃsena rohatu ||
english: Let hair be joined together with hair; let skin knit itself together with skin. Let your blood grow upon bone; let flesh grow upon flesh.

sanskrit: rohiṇī saṃrohiṇy asthnaḥ śīrṇasya rohiṇī | rohiṇyām ahni jātāsi rohiṇy asy oṣadhe ||
english: Rohiṇī is the fully healing one, Rohiṇī of broken bone. Born on the day of Rohiṇī (the lunar asterism), you are Rohiṇī, O herb.

sanskrit: yadi śīrṇaṃ yadi dyuttam asthi peṣṭraṃ ta ātmanaḥ | dhātā tat sarvaṃ kalpayāt saṃ dadhat paruṣā paruḥ ||
english: If the bone is broken, if it is shattered, the grinding agent against your own body — may Dhātṛ (the Divine Ordainer) set all that right, joining joint to joint.

sanskrit: yadi vajro visṛṣṭas tvāra kāṭaṃ patitvā yadi vā viriṣṭam | vṛkṣād vā yad avasad daśaśīrṣa ṛbhū rathasyeva saṃ dadhāmi te paruḥ ||
english: If a thunderbolt was hurled against you, or if it fell and pierced into the cut, or if you were shattered; or if you fell from a tree — O ten-headed, O Ṛbhu, I join your joints together as craftsmen join together the parts of a chariot.

sanskrit: ut tiṣṭha prehi sam adhāyi te paruḥ saṃ te dhātā dadhātu tanvo viriṣṭam | rathaḥ sucakraḥ supavir yathaiti sukhaḥ sunābhiḥ prati tiṣṭha evam ||
english: Rise up, go forward — your joint has been set in place; may Dhātṛ set together the broken part of your body. As a well-wheeled, well-felly'd, smooth, well-hubbed chariot rolls along — stand firm just so.
